sampling_model.design: Independent replicate wells are collected at fixed, known integer composition rows of \(M\), with exact raw-count addition and no unknown thinning or normalization. The two-row matrix \(M_0\) and both prescribed three-node inputs are synthetic prospective designs whose certification status remains open.
sampling_model.units: A unit is one replicate well containing exactly the declared number of independent cells of each labeled type; rowwise random splitting produces \(N_A\) training wells and \(N_B\) inference wells, both split sizes diverge, and the row fractions converge to a normalized rational probability vector \(\rho\) that is strictly positive for every sampled composition row.
sampling_model.treatment: For \(p\geq3\), the ordered embedding \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\) is fixed before analysis. Broad published-class membership is used only for labeled-DAG recovery. The interventions \(\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=1)\) and \(\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=2)\), and responses \(V_{i_Y}\) and \(V_{i_Z}\), are evaluated by truncated factorization only in the causally sufficient compact positive-polynomial Poisson subclass.
sampling_model.overlap: Positive Poisson roots and rates give full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\) in the strict benchmark subclass, so every parent configuration used in its truncated-factorization functional has positive observational probability. No such Poisson-root or full-support claim is imposed on the broader published CPCM class used only for graph recovery.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Pooled PGFs are empirical replicate-well averages; component PGFs use the full-rank log inverse; graph and parameter estimates use the deterministic lexicographic sample-split selector. The certifier always returns one of three statuses, but inference is activated only by \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\), after normalized positive row allocation, wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local nonsingularity, positive interiority clearance, tail control, and precision have all been verified.

Theorem 2 obtains component recovery under pairwise column independence for a generalized-hyperexponential approximation class.

Definition 3 specifies PT-SEM from direct observational count vectors; Theorem 12 identifies its DAG, thinning matrix, and node-wise exogenous distributions under (A1)--(A3), and Theorem 18 proves plug-in BIC selection consistency under (A1)--(A5).
Section 4.2 studies functional consistency under linear aggregation and gives affine ANM/PNL consequences; Section 4.3 concerns conditional-independence consistency.
The paper establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and covariance weighting for finite or continuum moments.
The article develops mathematically rigorous verification methods based on directed floating-point and interval arithmetic.
The article distinguishes rigorous from non-rigorous deterministic branch-and-bound and reviews sound interval relaxations and termination claims.
The paper combines Taylor-model enclosures with branch-and-bound for rigorous global search.
The paper constructs rigorous interval quasiconvex relaxations for self-validating constrained global optimization.
Theorems 2 and 4 certify approximate polynomial roots and common associated roots.
The paper optimizes network-tomography probe allocation using Fisher information.

tldr: Known linearly independent raw-count compositions recover unrestricted labeled type laws for arbitrary \(p\geq1\) by a logarithmic count-PGF inverse, with positive Poisson aliases proving necessity. For \(p\geq2\), any recovered count-valued law in the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class then has its labeled DAG identified; the three-coordinate condition is not part of graph recovery. Intervention contrasts and validation use the stricter compact positive-polynomial Poisson subclass. For \(p\geq3\), the headline is a finite sound tri-valued certifier: it always terminates, and only a \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) output verifies a rational chart-projection cover together with wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local Jacobian nonsingularity, interiority, PGF-tail, and designated-contrast precision bounds. The finite-grid theorem separately proves existence of some finite rational grid and cover with positive exact margins; it does not certify either prescribed synthetic input. Pointwise sample-split Wald inference is conditional on certification, the capped certified-design frontier is finite, and the three-node base/conditional-refinement benchmark status remains open.

project_justification.gap: Transform inversion, Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin's direct-law CPCM theorem, and validated-numerics methods are established separately. Their CPCM result identifies a graph from a direct count-valued joint law for \(p\geq2\), but it does not recover labeled type laws through known multi-composition pools; existing validated-numerics results do not jointly propagate infinite-support PGF tails through graph exclusion, remote within-graph separation, local chart injectivity, Jacobian regularity, covariance, and intervention precision.
project_justification.niche: Prospective known-composition designs need a proof-producing bridge from aggregate raw-count laws to labeled cellular laws and, already for \(p\geq2\), to the broadest justified graph class, with the \(p\geq3\) embedding reserved for intervention contrasts and with inference confined to a compact certifiable polynomial subclass.
project_justification.fill: The project composes the arbitrary-dimensional rank frontier with published pairwise-identifiable CPCM DAG recovery for \(p\geq2\), proves causal minimality of the strict positive-polynomial benchmark directly from its positive edge coefficients, and supplies for \(p\geq3\) an always-terminating one-sided-sound certifier plus a finite capped design frontier. Relative eventual certification is proved only under explicit strict exact slack and uniform convergence of all numerical controls; no prescribed synthetic input is claimed to meet those premises.

related_work: Shih--Hero is credited for logarithmic transform inversion of independent additive components; the integer-multiplicity multivariate count-PGF recovery map and positive unrestricted converse are derived here. Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin Definitions 9--10 describe the causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM setting, and their Lemma 11 identifies a labeled DAG from a direct joint law. Composing that result with labeled full-rank unpooling gives graph recovery for \(p\geq2\), without any ordered three-coordinate embedding or Poisson source restriction. The positive-polynomial Poisson subclass is shown, edge by edge, to be causally minimal and pairwise identifiable rather than acquiring those properties by definition; only intervention, finite-grid, certificate, and Wald layers use that stricter subclass. Carrasco--Florens and Newey--McFadden supply finite-moment minimum-distance ingredients. Rump, Kearfott, and Berz--Makino motivate validated arithmetic, interval global search, and Taylor enclosures. The new validation step jointly carries analytic Poisson-PGF tails through wrong-graph exclusion, the corrected one-sided remote-subset branch, rational chart covers, Jacobian and covariance checks, and designated causal precision. Its relative eventual-certification theorem is conditional on strict exact slack and convergent controls, not an assertion about the two fixed synthetic runs.
interpretation: Full column rank first identifies each labeled cellular observational law; it does not define a graph or an intervention. For \(p\geq2\), the recovered law identifies a labeled DAG on the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable CPCM class. The condition \(p\geq3\) and the fixed ordered embedding \(\iota\) enter only when selecting one treatment and two distinct response coordinates. Those intervention contrasts require the narrower causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass, whose full support identifies the kernels in the truncated factorization. The certificate handle enumerates the declared finite design class, records all three statuses, and promotes only \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) inputs to the Pareto comparison. Fixed controls always terminate but can remain undecided. Along a control sequence, eventual certification follows only from the separately stated strict-slack and uniform-convergence hypotheses.
technical_internal_limitation: The leaf ceiling and outward-rounded operation bound are unconditional finite ceilings, not efficiency guarantees. The \(27\)-point floating-point pilot and its two pointwise Jacobian singular values certify neither compact-box graph separation nor remote identification, chart coverage, tails, covariance, or useful contrast precision. Compactness converts strict exact slack into eventual positivity of sufficiently accurate lower enclosures, and the corrected remote rule permits a boundary-straddling box to pass from positive moment distance alone. That result is relative: without the stipulated strict margins and convergent truncation, Taylor, subdivision, and rounding controls, the procedure may return \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\). Neither fixed synthetic input currently has a validated proof object.
honest_scope: Unrestricted rank recovery and stability apply for arbitrary \(p\geq1\). Labeled-DAG transfer applies for \(p\geq2\) to recovered laws in the published causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable count-valued CPCM class and imposes neither a Poisson source law nor a three-coordinate embedding. Intervention contrasts, finite-grid construction, certification, and Wald inference are confined to the compact causally sufficient positive-polynomial Poisson subclass and, for the designated contrasts, require \(p\geq3\) and fixed \(\iota\). Certification is always terminating and one-sided sound but may be undecided. Eventual certification is conditional on strict positive exact graph, remote, chart, Jacobian, interiority, algebraic, and precision margins together with uniform numerical convergence; it certifies neither prescribed benchmark by itself. Covariance and Wald claims additionally require normalized strictly positive row fractions and give pointwise, not uniform post-selection, coverage. No claim covers unknown thinning, normalization, composition error, shared-well dependence, hidden types, high-dimensional growth, or biologically calibrated coefficient boxes.

assumptions.condition: The integer composition matrix \(M\) is fixed and known before replicate wells are observed.
Each observed well is the coordinatewise raw-count sum \(B_{ji}=\sum_{r=1}^{K}\sum_{c=1}^{M_{jr}}V_{jirc}\).
Within each pooled well, the cellular count vectors \(V_{jirc}\) are mutually independent.
For every type \(r\), each \(V_{jirc}\) has law \(P_r\) across composition rows and replicates.
The pooled count vectors \(B_{ji}\) are independent across distinct replicate wells.

novel.justification: Any assay measuring at least three coordinates admits a prespecified exposure coordinate and two distinct response coordinates; this domain restriction belongs only to the causal-certificate layer and leaves unrestricted law recovery unchanged.

assumptions.condition: For each type \(r\), the exogenous variables in the structural representation associated with \(d_r\) are jointly independent.

For every type \(r\), every root \(s\) in \(d_r\) has law \(\operatorname{Pois}(\alpha_{rs})\) with \(\alpha_{rs}>0\), while every non-root \(s\) has conditional kernel \(\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda_{rs,\theta})\) with \(\lambda_{rs,\theta}(v)=\alpha_{rs}+\sum_{k\in\operatorname{pa}_{d_r}(s)}b_{rsk}v_k^{q_{sk}}\) and strictly positive root and declared-edge coefficients.

novel.justification: This paper maintains a stricter Poisson-root positive-polynomial Poisson-DAG subclass as a transparent synthetic and prospective-design benchmark. Source-node Poissonity is imposed here; the broader CPCM framework permits arbitrary source-node laws.

assumptions.condition: Every directed parent--child pair and every admissible nondescendant conditioning set satisfy pairwise identifiability in the sense of Definition 10 of Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin.

Each \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\) and \(\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol d}\) is a prespecified compact rational rectangle, with \(\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol d}\subset\operatorname{int}(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d})\), and with strictly positive root and declared-edge coefficient lower endpoints.

novel.justification: A finite box is a prospective design input that can be calibrated from independent pilot assays; positive lower endpoints describe modules screened to exclude silent roots and vanishing candidate edges. The numerical box used below is only synthetic and is not asserted to be biologically calibrated.

assumptions.condition: The exponent array \(q\) is fixed before observing wells and has positive integer entries for every possible ordered edge.

novel.justification: Fixed low-order exponents encode a prespecified nonlinear benchmark and make finite validation possible. They can be chosen from external mechanistic restrictions, but the three-node exponent pattern below is explicitly synthetic.

assumptions.condition: The allocation satisfies \(\rho\in\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) with \(\rho_j>0\) for every row, and for each split \(S\in\{A,B\}\), \(n_{Sj}/N_S\to\rho_j\) for every composition row \(j\).
The finite-grid weight \(W\) is fixed and positive definite.

When \(p\geq3\) and the ordered embedding \(\iota\) is fixed, every reported scalar component \(\tau_{i_Y,r}\) and \(\tau_{i_Z,r}\) has strictly positive asymptotic variance at \(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\)
definitions.construction: Count one primitive operation for each exact rational addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, comparison, dyadic floor or ceiling, and integer-table update; an interval operation counts all of its endpoint primitives, and fixed-order fraction-free elimination, \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\), and matrix solves are expanded into these primitives. The deterministic rank, chart, Krawczyk, \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\), covariance, and sandwich routines use at most \(256(J+K+d_\star+KL)^3\) further primitives per leaf. Define \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)=P_{\mathrm{ar}}N_{\mathrm{leaf}}\{C_{\mathrm{rec}}+256(J+K+d_\star+KL)^3\}\). The displayed loop bounds and the fixed recurrence orders therefore give this literal finite ceiling on every counted operation, including unsuccessful precision passes; the bound is deliberately coarse and makes no polynomial-time claim.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{cert}}\)

Record every tri-valued status and its receipt, propagate the directed-rounding Taylor models and recursive Poisson tails through wrong-graph exclusion, one-sided remote-pair certification, local chart injectivity, Jacobian nonsingularity, covariance inversion, and designated-contrast precision, and retain as frontier candidates only nondominated inputs whose status is \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\). Inputs with status \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\) or \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\) remain recorded and are not promoted to certified designs.

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)<K\), every choice in \(\mathfrak A(M,a,\Lambda,u,\epsilon)\) produces two distinct labeled collections of full-support component laws whose row-wise pooled laws are identical.
statements.justification: This supplies a nonboundary necessity witness for the exact rank frontier.
statements.gap: Shih--Hero provides the high-level additive transform-inversion precedent but does not state this positive nullspace alias for arbitrary rank-deficient integer compositions.
statements.consumer: It shows that replication at unchanged composition rows cannot repair a rank-deficient prospective design.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(\operatorname{rank}(M)<K\).  Then there is \(0\ne a\in\ker(M)\).  Fix positive intensities \(\lambda_{rd}\) and \(0\ne u\in[0,\infty)^p\), and choose the nonzero \(\epsilon\) required by \(\mathrm{def{:}positive\text{-}poisson\text{-}alias}\).  For every \(r,d\),
\[
\lambda_{rd}(\epsilon)
\geq\lambda_{rd}-|\epsilon a_ru_d|
>\frac{\lambda_{rd}}2>0. \tag{7}
\]
Thus the baseline and perturbed type laws are both products of positive Poisson masses and have full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\).  Since \(a\ne0\) and \(u\ne0\), some product \(a_ru_d\) is nonzero, so those two labeled collections are distinct.

Under exact additive pooling and cell independence, the pooled coordinate \(d\) in row \(j\) is Poisson with intensity
\[
\sum_{r=1}^KM_{jr}\lambda_{rd}(\epsilon)
=\sum_{r=1}^KM_{jr}\lambda_{rd}
+\epsilon (Ma)_ju_d
=\sum_{r=1}^KM_{jr}\lambda_{rd}. \tag{8}
\]
All pooled coordinates are independent in both constructions.  Equation (8) therefore makes their entire row-wise pooled laws identical.  Independent replication and type invariance place both constructions in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\), completing the witness.

statements.statement: On \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\), the pooling map \(\mathscr A_M\) is injective for every labeled \(K\)-tuple \((P_1,\ldots,P_K)\in\mathcal P(\mathbb N_0^p)^K\) if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\). Under full column rank, \((G_1(z),\ldots,G_K(z))^{\mathsf T}=\mathscr R_M(H)(z)\) for every \(z\in(0,1]^p\), and PGF coefficient uniqueness recovers every \(P_r\).
statements.justification: The theorem gives the exact acquisition boundary before causal restrictions or finite-grid estimation are imposed.
statements.gap: Shih--Hero supplies the source-verified high-level idea of transform inversion for independent additive link delays; this theorem credits that idea, derives the displayed count-PGF recovery map, and adds the unrestricted multivariate count-law if-and-only-if frontier with a positive converse family.
statements.consumer: A prospective bulk-mixture study can determine whether its chosen composition rows identify labeled type laws before collecting replicates.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(z\in(0,1]^p\), \(z^V>0\) almost surely, so \(G_r(z)>0\).  Exact additive pooling, mutual cell independence, and type invariance give
\[
H_j(z)
=\mathbb E\!\left[
z^{\sum_{r,c}V_{jirc}}\right]
=\prod_{r=1}^KG_r(z)^{M_{jr}}. \tag{9}
\]
Consequently, with coordinatewise real logarithms,
\[
\log H(z)=M\log G(z). \tag{10}
\]
This is the count-PGF instance of the log-transform linearization credited to the cited Shih--Hero transform precedent.

If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), the Moore--Penrose inverse satisfies
\[
M^+M=(M^{\mathsf T}M)^{-1}M^{\mathsf T}M=I_K.
\]
Multiplying (10) and exponentiating coordinatewise proves
\[
G(z)=\exp\{M^+\log H(z)\}=\mathscr R_M(H)(z). \tag{11}
\]
Thus equality of pooled-law tuples implies equality of every component PGF on \((0,1)^p\).  To see directly that this identifies the law, subtract two component PGFs.  Fix \(p-1\) coordinates in \((0,1)\), view the difference as an absolutely convergent one-variable power series, and apply the continuation-and-least-nonzero-coefficient argument proved in the regularity lemma.  Its coefficients, which are power series in the remaining coordinates, vanish; repeating coordinate by coordinate shows that every coefficient vanishes.  Since the coefficient of \(z^v\) is \(P_r(\{v\})\), the component laws coincide.  Hence \(\mathscr A_M\) is injective.

Conversely, when \(\operatorname{rank}(M)<K\), the proved positive-Poisson alias lemma gives two distinct labeled full-support component-law tuples in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\) having identical pooled laws.  Therefore \(\mathscr A_M\) is not injective.  This establishes both directions and the explicit recovery map.

statements.statement: Every member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\) has full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\), is causally sufficient, and is pairwise identifiable in the sense of Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin; hence it belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\).
statements.justification: The proposition now proves full support, causal sufficiency, and causal minimality directly; each positive polynomial edge changes a positive-probability conditional Poisson kernel, and the nonexceptional increasing rate verifies the maintained pairwise condition.
statements.gap: The published CPCM definitions do not themselves verify causal minimality or pairwise identifiability for this paper's strict positive-polynomial benchmark.
statements.consumer: It validates that every graph and parameter box searched by the reusable certificate lies inside the broader direct-law identifiable CPCM class.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), a type \(r\), and a topological ordering of its DAG \(d_r\).  At a root \(s\), the mass \(e^{-\alpha_{rs}}\alpha_{rs}^{v_s}/v_s!\) is positive for every \(v_s\in\mathbb N_0\), because \(\alpha_{rs}>0\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}poisson\text{-}root\text{-}positive\text{-}polynomial\text{-}dag}\).  At a non-root, the same assumption gives
\[
\lambda_{rs,\theta}(v)=\alpha_{rs}+
\sum_{k\in\operatorname{pa}_{d_r}(s)}b_{rsk}v_k^{q_{sk}}>0,
\]
because the intercept and every declared-edge coefficient are strictly positive and the parent counts are nonnegative.  Hence every conditional Poisson mass is positive.  The DAG factorization therefore yields
\[
 p_{r,\theta}(v)=\prod_{s=1}^{p}
 p_{rs,\theta}\bigl(v_s\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{d_r}(s)}\bigr)>0
 \qquad(v\in\mathbb N_0^p). \tag{1}
\]
Thus the observational law has full support.

For causal sufficiency, let \((U_{rs})_{s=1}^p\) be mutually independent \(\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) variables.  In topological order, define each \(V_s\) as the generalized inverse of its stipulated root or conditional Poisson distribution evaluated at \(U_{rs}\).  The probability integral transform for a discrete distribution shows that the resulting conditional kernel is exactly \(p_{rs,\theta}\).  The exogenous variables are jointly independent, so this construction is a causally sufficient acyclic structural representation of (1).

We next prove causal minimality rather than assuming it.  Fix a declared edge \(k\to s\), and fix all other parents of \(s\) at zero.  Full support in (1) makes each of the conditioning events
\[
 \{V_k=x,\ V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)\setminus\{k\}}=0\},
 \qquad x\in\mathbb N_0,
\]
have positive probability.  On those events the conditional rate of \(V_s\) is
\[
 \lambda_s(x)=\alpha_{rs}+b_{rsk}x^{q_{sk}}. \tag{2}
\]
By \(b_{rsk}>0\) and \(q_{sk}\in\mathbb N\),
\(\lambda_s(1)-\lambda_s(0)=b_{rsk}>0\).  In particular,
\[
 \Pr(V_s=0\mid V_k=1,V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)\setminus\{k\}}=0)
 =e^{-\alpha_{rs}-b_{rsk}}
 \ne e^{-\alpha_{rs}}
 =\Pr(V_s=0\mid V_k=0,V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)\setminus\{k\}}=0). \tag{3}
\]
Thus \(V_s\) is not conditionally independent of \(V_k\) given its other parents.  This holds for every declared edge, so deletion of any edge destroys the Markov factorization; equivalently, the generating DAG is causally minimal.

It remains to verify pairwise identifiability.  Fix the same edge and an admissible set \(S\) satisfying
\[
 \operatorname{pa}_{d_r}(s)\setminus\{k\}
 \subseteq S\subseteq
 \operatorname{nd}_{d_r}(s)\setminus\{k,s\}.
\]
By (1), \(\Pr(V_S=0)>0\) and
\(\Pr(V_k=x,V_S=0)>0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb N_0\).  The local Markov property of the displayed DAG factorization implies that, after all other parents have been fixed, additionally conditioning on nondescendants that are not parents does not change the child kernel.  Hence under \(V_S=0\) the conditional rate remains (2), which is strictly increasing and unbounded.  By the frozen \(\mathrm{lem{:}poisson\text{-}cpcm\text{-}reversibility}\), failure of bivariate Poisson-CPCM direction identification can occur only when the forward rate is \(\exp(ax+b)\) with \(a<0\), a strictly decreasing function.  Equation (2) cannot have that form.  The conditioned pair is therefore identifiable.  Since the edge and admissible set were arbitrary, the maintained pairwise-identifiability requirement holds; if there are no edges it is vacuous.

We have proved full support, causal sufficiency, causal minimality, and the pairwise-identifiability condition for every type.  These are precisely the relevant membership requirements of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}cpcm\text{-}class}\), so the asserted inclusion follows.

statements.statement: Set \(p=3\) and fix the ordered embedding \(\iota(X)=i_X=1\), \(\iota(Y)=i_Y=2\), and \(\iota(Z)=i_Z=3\). For each type \(r\) in the fixed synthetic protocol, the truncated-factorization contrasts satisfy \(\tau_{i_Y,r}=3\) and \(\tau_{i_Z,r}=25\).
statements.justification: This checks the designated-coordinate intervention arithmetic in the synthetic three-node application.
statements.gap: The calculation is an application check and is not presented as a theorem-level novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It supplies auditable contrast targets for the finite-input certificate without treating the synthetic box as biological calibration.
statements.proof_tex:
Under the fixed protocol and an intervention \(V_1=x\), the second node has
\[
V_2\mid\operatorname{do}(V_1=x)\sim
\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda_x),\qquad \lambda_x=1+x^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
\mathbb E[V_2\mid\operatorname{do}(V_1=x)]=\lambda_x.
\]
The third conditional mean is \(1+x+V_2^2\).  Since a Poisson variable of mean \(\lambda\) has second moment \(\lambda+\lambda^2\), iterated expectation gives
\[
\mathbb E[V_3\mid\operatorname{do}(V_1=x)]
=1+x+\lambda_x+\lambda_x^2. \tag{14}
\]
At \(x=1\), the two displayed means are \(2\) and \(8\); at \(x=2\), they are \(5\) and \(33\).  Subtracting the \(x=1\) values from the \(x=2\) values gives
\[
\tau_{i_Y,r}=5-2=3,\qquad
\tau_{i_Z,r}=33-8=25.
\]
The conditional kernels other than that of the intervened coordinate are exactly those retained by the declared truncated factorization, so these are the causal contrasts in the proposition for each type.

statements.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\), fix the ordered injection \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\), and consider a pooled experiment in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\). If \(((P_{r,\theta_r},D_r,\theta_r))_{r=1}^{K}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), then the pooled-law tuple \(\mathscr A_M((P_{r,\theta_r})_{r=1}^{K})\) identifies the \(\iota\)-indexed intervention-contrast vector \(\boldsymbol\tau=((\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}))_{r=1}^{K}\) through the truncated-factorization functional at \(V_{i_X}\).
statements.justification: After the separate \(p\geq2\) graph-transfer theorem, this result uses \(p\geq3\) only to transfer an identified polynomial-CPCM law and graph to one treatment and two response contrasts.
statements.gap: The published direct-law CPCM theorem identifies the DAG but neither unpools labeled type laws nor proves that the strict polynomial subclass's support, modular factorization, and moments make the designated contrast functional identifiable.
statements.consumer: It states the intervention-effect output available to a prospective known-composition bulk assay after broad graph recovery, without extending finite-grid, certification, or Wald claims beyond the strict polynomial subclass.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a type \(r\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\), and let \(V_r=(V_{r1},\ldots,V_{rp})\) denote a generic cellular vector with law \(P_{r,\theta_r}\).  The endogenous variables are the labeled count coordinates \(V_{r1},\ldots,V_{rp}\); the treatment is \(V_{r i_X}\), and the two outcomes are \(V_{r i_Y}\) and \(V_{r i_Z}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}three\text{-}designated\text{-}coordinates}\) and injectivity of \(\iota\) ensure that these three coordinates exist and are pairwise distinct.

First separate recovery of an observational law from identification of the causal contrast.  Let
\[
H(z)=(H_1(z),\ldots,H_J(z))^{\mathsf T},\qquad z\in(0,1]^p,
\]
be the vector of observable row probability generating functions.  Membership in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\), the assumed equality \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), and \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}frontier}\) give
\[
\begin{pmatrix}G_1(z)\\ \vdots\\ G_K(z)\end{pmatrix}
=\mathscr R_M(H)(z)
=\exp\!\left\{M^+\log H(z)\right\},
\qquad z\in(0,1]^p. \tag{1}
\]
The logarithms in (1) are defined because \(z^{B_{ji}}>0\) pointwise on this domain and hence \(H_j(z)>0\).  The same theorem's probability-generating-function coefficient uniqueness conclusion therefore identifies each labeled observational law \(P_{r,\theta_r}\).  Equation (1) is an equality between an observable recovery functional and observational probability generating functions; it neither defines nor presupposes an intervention distribution.

By \(\mathrm{prop{:}polynomial\text{-}class\text{-}inclusion}\), every recovered component in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\) has full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\), is causally sufficient, and lies in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\).  Since \(p\geq3\) implies \(p\geq2\), \(\mathrm{thm{:}cpcm\text{-}graph\text{-}transfer}\) then identifies its labeled generating DAG \(D_r\).  This graph-recovery step uses neither the choice of \(i_X,i_Y,i_Z\) nor the intervention contrast; those enter only below.

Full support supplies the overlap needed to recover all observational kernels that occur after intervention.  For any vertex \(s\) and any parent configuration
\(a\in\mathbb N_0^{|\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)|}\), choose a complete vector \(v\in\mathbb N_0^p\) whose parent coordinates equal \(a\).  Full support gives \(P_{r,\theta_r}(V_r=v)>0\), whence
\[
P_{r,\theta_r}\!\left(V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a\right)
\geq P_{r,\theta_r}(V_r=v)>0. \tag{2}
\]
Consequently the identified law and identified graph determine, for every \(v_s\in\mathbb N_0\),
\[
p_{rs,\theta_r}(v_s\mid a)
=\frac{P_{r,\theta_r}\!\left(V_{rs}=v_s,
V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a\right)}
{P_{r,\theta_r}\!\left(V_{r,\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=a\right)}. \tag{3}
\]
The denominator is strictly positive by (2); when \(s\) is a root, the conditioning configuration is empty and its probability is one.  Thus no positivity condition is being silently imposed on only observationally occurring parent values: every finite parent configuration, including those induced by setting \(V_{r i_X}=1\) or \(2\), is covered by (2).

We next relate these observational kernels to the causal target.  Causal sufficiency and the acyclic CPCM semantics give a modular recursive system in a topological ordering of \(D_r\), with each node generated from its parents according to the kernel in (3) and with no latent common cause between node assignments.  Surgical intervention at \(V_{r i_X}\) replaces only that node's assignment by the constant \(x\in\{1,2\}\).  The chain rule in the resulting recursive system therefore gives
\[
Q_{r,x}(v_{-i_X})
:=P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=x)}(v_{-i_X})
=\prod_{s\ne i_X}
p_{rs,\theta_r}\!\left(v_s\mid
v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}\right)
\Big|_{v_{i_X}=x}. \tag{4}
\]
This is the truncated factorization in \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}factorization\text{-}effect}\), now derived from the surgical-intervention semantics.  It is a probability mass function.  Indeed, its factors are nonnegative, so Tonelli's theorem permits iterated summation; summing the nonintervened vertices in reverse topological order removes at each step a terminal node's conditional mass function, whose sum is one.  After finitely many such steps, \(\sum_{v_{-i_X}}Q_{r,x}(v_{-i_X})=1\).

It remains to verify that the expectations defining the contrast are finite.  If \(N\mid\lambda\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)\), then for every integer \(\ell\geq0\), direct summation yields
\[
\mathbb E[(N)_{\ell}\mid\lambda]
=\sum_{n=\ell}^{\infty}
\frac{n!}{(n-\ell)!}e^{-\lambda}\frac{\lambda^n}{n!}
=\lambda^{\ell}, \tag{5}
\]
where \((N)_{\ell}=N(N-1)\cdots(N-\ell+1)\) and \((N)_0=1\).  The finite identity
\(N^m=\sum_{\ell=0}^{m}S(m,\ell)(N)_{\ell}\), where \(S(m,\ell)\) is a Stirling number of the second kind, shows from (5) that every conditional raw moment of \(N\) is a finite polynomial in \(\lambda\).

Under either intervention, the fixed coordinate \(V_{r i_X}=x\) has moments of every order.  Every nonintervened root has a positive finite Poisson rate by \(\mathrm{ass{:}poisson\text{-}root\text{-}positive\text{-}polynomial\text{-}dag}\), so (5) gives all of its moments.  Suppose inductively in a topological ordering that every parent of a nonintervened non-root \(s\) has moments of every order.  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}poisson\text{-}root\text{-}positive\text{-}polynomial\text{-}dag}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}positive\text{-}exponents}\),
\[
\lambda_{rs,\theta_r}
=\alpha_{rs}+
\sum_{k\in\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}
b_{rsk}V_{rk}^{q_{sk}}, \tag{6}
\]
where all displayed coefficients are finite and every \(q_{sk}\) is a positive integer.  For an integer \(m\geq1\), put \(h=1+|\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)|\).  Convexity of \(t\mapsto t^m\) on \([0,\infty)\) gives
\[
\lambda_{rs,\theta_r}^{m}
\leq h^{m-1}\!\left(
\alpha_{rs}^{m}+
\sum_{k\in\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}
b_{rsk}^{m}V_{rk}^{m q_{sk}}
\right). \tag{7}
\]
The right-hand side has finite expectation by the induction hypothesis, also when one parent is the fixed intervention coordinate.  Equations (5)--(7) imply that \(V_{rs}\) has moments of every order.  Induction over the finite DAG proves, in particular,
\[
\sum_{v_{-i_X}}(v_{i_Y}+v_{i_Z})Q_{r,x}(v_{-i_X})<\infty,
\qquad x\in\{1,2\}. \tag{8}
\]

Define, only now, the observable-law functional
\[
\Phi_r(P_{r,\theta_r},D_r)
=\sum_{v_{-i_X}}(v_{i_Y},v_{i_Z})
\left\{
\prod_{s\ne i_X}p_{rs,\theta_r}\!\left(v_s\mid
v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}\right)\Big|_{v_{i_X}=2}
-
\prod_{s\ne i_X}p_{rs,\theta_r}\!\left(v_s\mid
v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}\right)\Big|_{v_{i_X}=1}
\right\}. \tag{9}
\]
Both sums in (9) are finite by (8).  Every kernel in (9) is identified by (3), and every graph index in (9) is identified by \(\mathrm{thm{:}cpcm\text{-}graph\text{-}transfer}\); hence \(\Phi_r\) is determined by the pooled-law tuple through (1).  On the other hand, substituting the causally derived equality (4) into (9) proves, rather than defines, the equality
\[
\Phi_r(P_{r,\theta_r},D_r)
=\mathbb E_{P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=2)}}
[(V_{r i_Y},V_{r i_Z})]
-\mathbb E_{P_{r,\theta_r}^{\operatorname{do}(V_{r i_X}=1)}}
[(V_{r i_Y},V_{r i_Z})]
=\bigl(\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}\bigr). \tag{10}
\]
Applying (10) to each labeled type \(r=1,\ldots,K\) identifies \(\boldsymbol\tau\).  Thus the full-rank observable recovery map first identifies the component laws, the broad CPCM result identifies their labeled DAGs, and only the polynomial-CPCM support, modularity, and moment conditions are used to identify the fixed truncated-factorization intervention contrasts.

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\) and \(\delta<\beta\), then \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal Z_\eta}\lVert M^{+}\log\widetilde H(z)-\log G(z)\rVert_2\leq E_M\), \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal Z_\eta}\lVert\mathscr R_M(\widetilde H)(z)-G(z)\rVert_2\leq e^{E_M}E_M\), and \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal Z_\eta}\max_r|\mathscr R_M(\widetilde H)_r(z)/G_r(z)-1|\leq e^{E_M}-1\).
statements.justification: The result separates qualitative rank from operational amplification through both \(\lVert M^{+}\rVert_2\) and pooled-PGF attenuation.
statements.gap: Shih--Hero provides the high-level independent-additive transform-inversion precedent but does not supply this multivariate lower-envelope perturbation bound for designed count pools.
statements.consumer: It screens compositions and grid locations before running the more expensive validated certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(z\in\mathcal Z_\eta\).  Monotonicity of \(z^v\) in every coordinate gives
\[
G_r(z)\geq G_r(\eta,\ldots,\eta)=\gamma_r.
\]
Equation (9) then gives \(H_j(z)\geq\prod_r\gamma_r^{M_{jr}}\geq\beta\).  Since every coordinate error is at most its Euclidean norm,
\[
\widetilde H_j(z)\geq H_j(z)-\delta\geq\beta-\delta>0. \tag{17}
\]
The scalar mean-value theorem for the logarithm and (17) imply
\[
|\log\widetilde H_j(z)-\log H_j(z)|
\leq\frac{|\widetilde H_j(z)-H_j(z)|}{\beta-\delta}.
\]
Taking Euclidean norms and using the definition of \(\delta\) yields
\[
\|\log\widetilde H(z)-\log H(z)\|_2
\leq\frac{\delta}{\beta-\delta}. \tag{18}
\]
Under full column rank, the rank-frontier identity is
\(M^+\log H(z)=\log G(z)\).  Submultiplicativity applied to (18) proves
\[
\|M^+\log\widetilde H(z)-\log G(z)\|_2
\leq \|M^+\|_2\frac{\delta}{\beta-\delta}=E_M. \tag{19}
\]

Write \(\Delta=M^+\log\widetilde H-\log G\).  Since \(0<G_r\leq1\),
\[
|\exp(\log G_r+\Delta_r)-G_r|
=G_r|e^{\Delta_r}-1|
\leq e^{|\Delta_r|}|\Delta_r|
\leq e^{E_M}|\Delta_r|.
\]
Summing squares proves the second asserted bound.  Division by \(G_r>0\) gives
\[
\left|\frac{\mathscr R_M(\widetilde H)_r}{G_r}-1\right|
=|e^{\Delta_r}-1|
\leq e^{|\Delta_r|}-1\leq e^{E_M}-1.
\]
All bounds are independent of \(z\); taking the stated suprema completes the proof.

statements.statement: For any fixed nonempty finite \(\mathfrak G\), nonempty compact boxes, exponent array, and nonempty open \(\mathcal O\subset(0,1)^p\), there are a finite rational \(\mathcal T\subset\mathcal O\), a rational \(r_{\mathrm{id}}>0\), and a valid finite rational chart-projection cover \(\mathscr C\) such that \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0\), \(\kappa_{\mathcal T}>0\), \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})>0\), and \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)>0\). Here \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\) when \(|\mathfrak G|=1\), and \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\) when its remote pair set is empty. Consequently each within-graph moment map is globally injective; this uses local chart strong monotonicity and remote separation, not the Jacobian margin alone.
statements.justification: This establishes existence of a finite transform design with distinct global and local certificates.
statements.gap: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin supplies neither a finite PGF grid nor quantitative global-injectivity and Jacobian margins over compact boxes.
statements.consumer: It supplies the consistency check that the reusable certificate is searching for a nonvacuous finite-input object.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a graph tuple \(\boldsymbol d\) and write
\[
 F_{\boldsymbol d}(\theta,z)
 =\bigl(G_{r,\theta_r}(z)\bigr)_{r=1}^{K}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}polynomial\text{-}pgf\text{-}regularity}\), this map and its coefficient derivative are continuous.  For a unit parameter direction \(v\), injectivity of the coefficient-to-law differential implies that the signed derivative measure is nonzero.  If its PGF were zero on the nonempty open set \(\mathcal O\), the successive one-variable power-series uniqueness argument used in (12) would make all its coefficients zero.  Therefore, for every \((\theta,v)\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\times\mathbb S^{d_{\boldsymbol d}-1}\), some \(z\in\mathcal O\) satisfies
\[
 D_\theta F_{\boldsymbol d}(\theta,z)v\ne0. \tag{13}
\]
Continuity makes the same point work on a neighborhood of \((\theta,v)\).  The parameter-box--unit-sphere product is compact, so finitely many such neighborhoods cover it.  Stacking the corresponding finitely many evaluations gives a Jacobian with trivial kernel for every \(\theta\).  Repeating this over the finite graph set and taking the union of the evaluation points yields a finite preliminary grid on which
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}}
 \sigma_{\min}(J_{\boldsymbol d}(\theta))>0
 \qquad(\boldsymbol d\in\mathfrak G), \tag{14}
\]
because the smallest singular value is continuous on each compact box.

We construct the local charts explicitly.  At any \(\theta\), (14) gives the left inverse
\[
 L_\theta=(J(\theta)^{\mathsf T}J(\theta))^{-1}J(\theta)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Choose a rational matrix \(P_\theta\) sufficiently close to \(L_\theta\).  Continuity then gives a relative open neighborhood \(U_\theta\) and \(c_\theta>0\) such that
\[
 \frac{P_\theta J(\vartheta)+J(\vartheta)^{\mathsf T}P_\theta^{\mathsf T}}2
 \succeq c_\theta I
 \qquad(\vartheta\in U_\theta). \tag{15}
\]
Choose a finite subcover \(U_1,\ldots,U_m\).  If some \(U_i\) is the whole parameter box, retain that one set and choose any positive scale small enough for the construction below.  Otherwise, to avoid importing a covering assertion without proof, put
\[
 d(x)=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}
 \operatorname{dist}\bigl(x,\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\setminus U_i\bigr),
\]
Every complement is then nonempty and relatively closed, so each displayed distance is continuous.  Every \(x\) lies in some \(U_i\), hence \(d(x)>0\); compactness gives \(\delta=\min_xd(x)>0\).  In the whole-box case choose \(\delta>0\) arbitrarily.  Partition the rational rectangle \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\) into finitely many closed rational boxes of Euclidean diameter below \(\delta/4\), and choose a positive rational \(r_{\boldsymbol d}<\delta/(4\sqrt{d_{\boldsymbol d}})\).  For each base box \(H\), in the nontrivial-cover case select an index \(i\) for which one point of \(H\) has distance at least \(\delta\) from \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\setminus U_i\), and in the whole-box case select its sole index.  Set
\[
 C_H=\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\cap
 \bigl(H+[-r_{\boldsymbol d},r_{\boldsymbol d}]^{d_{\boldsymbol d}}\bigr).
\]
The diameter bounds imply \(C_H\subset U_i\), so attach the rational projection \(P_i\).  The base boxes cover the parameter box.  Moreover, if \(\theta\in H\) and \(\|\theta-\theta'\|_2<r_{\boldsymbol d}\), then \(\theta,\theta'\in C_H\).  Taking a positive rational \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) below the finite minimum of the \(r_{\boldsymbol d}\)'s gives a valid finite rational chart-projection cover for every graph.

For \(\theta,\theta'\) in a common convex chart, let \(\Delta=\theta'-\theta\).  The fundamental theorem of calculus and (15) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \langle P\{m(\theta')-m(\theta)\},\Delta\rangle
 &=\int_0^1\Delta^{\mathsf T}PJ(\theta+t\Delta)\Delta\,dt\\
 &=\int_0^1\Delta^{\mathsf T}
 \frac{PJ+J^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}}2
 \Delta\,dt\\
 &\geq c_H\|\Delta\|_2^2.
\end{aligned} \tag{16}
\]
The minimum of the finitely many positive \(c_H\)'s is positive, proving the desired local strong-monotonicity margin.

It remains to add finitely many points for global separation.  For a fixed graph, the remote set
\[
 R_{\boldsymbol d}=\{(\theta,\theta')\in
 \Theta_{\boldsymbol d}^2:\|\theta-\theta'\|_2\geq r_{\mathrm{id}}\}
\]
is compact.  By within-graph law injectivity from \(\mathrm{lem{:}polynomial\text{-}pgf\text{-}regularity}\), each pair in this set has different laws and hence differs at some PGF evaluation in \(\mathcal O\), again by power-series uniqueness.  That strict inequality persists on a neighborhood of the pair.  A finite subcover of \(R_{\boldsymbol d}\) supplies finitely many separating points.  The same argument on each compact product \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\times\Theta_{\boldsymbol d'}\), \(\boldsymbol d\ne\boldsymbol d'\), uses the disjoint graph-law images from the regularity lemma and supplies finitely many wrong-graph separating points.  Union these with the Jacobian grid.  Appending coordinates preserves (14) and (16), after padding each projection with zero columns.  Positive definiteness of \(W\) then turns nonzero moment differences into positive squared \(W\)-distances.  Compactness and continuity give positive minima for every nonempty remote and wrong-graph comparison set.  The declared \(+\infty\) conventions cover empty sets.

All inequalities just obtained have positive uniform margins on finitely many compact sets.  Joint continuity in the finitely many evaluation points therefore permits a sufficiently small simultaneous perturbation without destroying any inequality or chart containment.  Rational points are dense in the open set \(\mathcal O\), so choose the perturbed evaluations rational and call their set \(\mathcal T\).  We have proved
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0,
 \qquad \kappa_{\mathcal T}>0,
 \qquad \Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})>0,
 \qquad \mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)>0. \tag{17}
\]
For any two within-graph parameters, (16) separates them if their distance is below \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\), and the remote bound separates them otherwise.  Thus every within-graph moment map is globally injective.  This last conclusion uses the chart and remote margins, not the Jacobian margin alone.

statements.statement: For \(p\geq3\), fixed \(\iota\), and finite \(\Xi\), the procedure terminates after at most \(G_{\#}2^{c_{\max}}+G_{\#}2^{b_{\max}}+(G_{\#}+\binom{G_{\#}}{2})4^{b_{\max}}\) chart or objective leaves and \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\) outward-rounded operations. It rejects \(\rho\notin\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) before covariance or required-well evaluation. A \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) output proves full rank; normalized allocation with \(\rho_j>0\) for every composition row entering the unpooling map; valid chart coverage; positive exact untruncated bounds \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\), \(\kappa_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\kappa_{\mathcal T}\), \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})\geq\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})\), and \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)\geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)\); positive interiority; the recorded tail and variance bounds; and \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq N_{\max}\). For an empty wrong-graph comparison or remote-pair set, the corresponding exact and certified bounds are \(+\infty\) and impose no numerical check. A \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\) output proves its named obstruction; \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\) makes no substantive claim.
statements.justification: This theorem proves unconditional finite termination and one-sided soundness of every certified or refuted output. The separate \(\mathrm{thm{:}relative\text{-}eventual\text{-}certification}\) supplies the only completeness statement, under explicit strict slack and convergent controls.
statements.gap: Existing validated-numerics results do not jointly propagate Poisson-PGF tails through wrong-graph, remote-subset, local-chart, covariance, and causal-precision tasks, and fixed finite controls need not decide them.
statements.consumer: It turns a declared prospective design into an auditable go, stop, or undecided result, while the relative companion theorem states exactly when refinement eventually yields go.
statements.proof_tex:
Every loop in \(\mathfrak C\) ranges over a finite graph set, a finite retained state set, finite multi-index and precision lists, and binary trees of prescribed depth.  A binary tree of depth \(d\) has at most \(2^d\) leaves; the stated product-box bound \(4^{b_{\max}}\) is a valid coarse ceiling.  Summing the chart, single-graph objective, same-graph remote-product, and unordered wrong-graph product trees gives at most
\[
 G_{\#}2^{c_{\max}}+G_{\#}2^{b_{\max}}
 +\left(G_{\#}+\binom{G_{\#}}2\right)4^{b_{\max}}. \tag{21}
\]
There are
\[
 P_{\mathrm{ar}}=1+
 \left\lceil\frac{b_{\mathrm{cap}}-b_0}{\Delta b}\right\rceil
\]
precision passes.  The literal recurrence and linear-algebra counts in \(\mathrm{def{:}arithmetic\text{-}complexity}\), multiplied by its leaf count including the terminal task, are exactly \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\).  This proves unconditional finite termination and both displayed ceilings.

We next prove enclosure validity.  For a conditional Poisson variable,
\[
 \mathbb E[V_s^m\mid V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)}]
 =\sum_{k=0}^{m}
 \left\{\begin{matrix}m\\k\end{matrix}\right\}\lambda_s^k.
\]
For \(h_s=1+|\operatorname{pa}(s)|\), convexity of \(x\mapsto x^k\) on \([0,\infty)\) gives
\[
 \left(\alpha_s+\sum_u b_{su}V_u^{q_{su}}\right)^k
 \leq h_s^{k-1}
 \left(\alpha_s^k+
 \sum_u b_{su}^kV_u^{q_{su}k}\right). \tag{22}
\]
Topological induction proves that each recursive \(U_{\boldsymbol d rs}(m)\) majorizes the corresponding raw moment.  Deleting the intervened kernel and substituting a fixed count leaves the same induction valid.

Direct differentiation of a Poisson log mass, using the strictly positive lower rate \(\lambda^-_{rs}\), bounds its first derivative by \(L_{e_t}\) and every higher derivative by the displayed \(L_\nu\).  The multivariate product rule and the complete-Bell recurrence then prove inductively that
\[
 |\partial^\nu p_\theta(v)|\leq p_\theta(v)D_\nu(v). \tag{23}
\]
For \(T_R=\{v:\text{some }v_s>R_s\}\), the union bound and
\(\mathbf1\{v_s>R_s\}\leq v_s^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}/(R_s+1)^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}\) give
\[
 \sum_{v\in T_R}|\partial^\nu p_\theta(v)|
 \leq\sum_s
 \frac{\mathcal U_{\boldsymbol d r}(D_\nu V_s^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}})}
 {(R_s+1)^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}}
 =E_{\boldsymbol d r,\nu}. \tag{24}
\]
Multiplication by \(V_{i_Y}+V_{i_Z}\) gives the stated intervention-and-contrast tail bound.  If \(a,b\in[0,1]\) and \(|a-\widetilde a|,|b-\widetilde b|\leq\varepsilon_0\), then
\[
 |ab-\widetilde a\widetilde b|
 \leq |a|\,|b-\widetilde b|+|\widetilde b|\,|a-\widetilde a|
 \leq2\varepsilon_0+\varepsilon_0^2, \tag{25}
\]
which validates the covariance-product enlargement.

Taylor's theorem gives, for \(x\geq0\),
\[
 \left|e^{-x}-\sum_{k=0}^{a}\frac{(-x)^k}{k!}\right|
 \leq\frac{x^{a+1}}{(a+1)!}. \tag{26}
\]
Thus the initial exponential interval is valid.  Induction through the Poisson, complete-Bell, multivariate Leibniz, and fixed Taylor recurrences preserves inclusion.  Equation (24) enlarges retained sums to cover the exact infinite sums.  Downward rounding of lower endpoints and upward rounding of upper endpoints preserve inclusion under each rational arithmetic operation; division is used only after its divisor interval excludes zero.  Consequently every recorded interval contains its exact untruncated target.

A positive lower endpoint for a wrong-graph objective therefore bounds the objective on its whole leaf.  For a remote-product leaf, the corrected rule also passes whenever the moment-distance lower endpoint is positive on the whole product box, whether or not the distance-constraint interval has a nonnegative lower endpoint.  Such positivity necessarily holds on the leaf's remote feasible subset.  Conversely, a leaf whose distance-constraint upper endpoint is negative contains no remote feasible point and is soundly discarded.  Passing leaves and discarded infeasible leaves cover the required product domain, so
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})
 \geq\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}}). \tag{27}
\]
The interval \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) tests respectively certify
\(J^{\mathsf T}J-u^2I\succ0\) and
\((PJ+J^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T})/2-uI\succ0\) throughout their boxes.  Chart coverage then gives
\[
 \kappa_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\kappa_{\mathcal T}>0,
 \qquad
 \mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)
 \geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)>0. \tag{28}
\]
Exact rational comparisons certify syntax, box validity, full rank, normalized positive row allocation, and positive inference-box clearance.  The covariance and sandwich enclosures, protected by nonzero denominator and positive-definiteness tests, give the recorded variance upper bounds.  Outward evaluation of the displayed formulas then proves \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq N_{\max}\).  Because the simplex check precedes all covariance and well calculations, a failed simplex is rejected at the stated stage.

For a collision test, the frozen \(\mathrm{lem{:}krawczyk\text{-}inclusion}\) gives a zero \(y\in X\) of the selected square projection.  The mean-value matrix between the center and \(y\) belongs to the Jacobian enclosure, so substituting \(F(y)=0\) in the Krawczyk expression shows \(y\in K(x,X)\).  Every omitted moment coordinate is enclosed by the singleton \([0,0]\) on that set, hence also vanishes at \(y\).  The full moment difference is zero, and the disjoint parameter factors give the recorded wrong-graph collision.  Exact rank defect, invalid boxes, and simplex failure are direct obstructions.  Thus every \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\) output proves its named obstruction.  An exhausted or failed test is assigned \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\), to which the definition attaches no substantive conclusion.  Empty comparison sets have their declared \(+\infty\) values and require no numerical test.  This proves every unconditional soundness assertion.

statements.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\), fix \(\iota\), and let \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)=\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\). Suppose the true pooled model has \(\boldsymbol D_0\in\mathfrak G\) and \(\theta_0\in\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol D_0}\), the normalized allocation obeys \(\rho\in\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) with \(\rho_j>0\) for every row and \(n_{Sj}/N_S\to\rho_j\) for \(S\in\{A,B\}\), and the weighting and nondegeneracy conditions hold. As \(\min(N_A,N_B)\to\infty\), the declared lexicographic selector satisfies \(\Pr(\widehat{\boldsymbol D}=\boldsymbol D_0)\to1\), while \(\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}-\boldsymbol\tau)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,V_\tau(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0;\iota))\). Plug-in covariance is consistent and scalar Wald intervals have pointwise coverage \(1-\alpha\). The conclusion separately uses certified wrong-graph separation, certified global within-graph uniqueness, certified local nonsingularity, certified positive inference-box clearance, the normalized row allocation, and the deterministic selector. Moreover \(\lVert\Sigma_g\rVert_2\leq\lVert\operatorname{diag}(g)\rVert_2^2\lVert M^+\rVert_2^2\lVert\operatorname{diag}(h)^{-1}\rVert_2^2\lVert\Sigma_h\rVert_2\).
statements.justification: The inference layer uses exactly the global, local, interior, selector, and covariance objects certified by the decision layer.
statements.gap: Chen--Cao--Bu and Carrasco--Florens provide transform-moment ingredients, but neither conditions graph-selected intervention inference on a matching validated global certificate with propagated precision bounds.
statements.consumer: A certified prospective benchmark obtains uncertainty from replicate wells without manufacturing pseudo-single-cell observations.
statements.proof_tex:
Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}stratified\text{-}pgf\text{-}limit}\) separately to the independent training and inference splits.  Certification supplies full column rank and the required positive normalized row fractions, so
\[
 \widehat g_A\overset p\longrightarrow g_0,
 \qquad
 \widehat g_B\overset p\longrightarrow g_0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt{N_B}(\widehat g_B-g_0)
 \Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_g). \tag{29}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}polynomial\text{-}pgf\text{-}regularity}\), every graph-box moment map is continuous and the true one is continuously differentiable near \(\theta_0\).  Since the graph set and boxes are finite and compact, and \(W\) is fixed, there is a finite constant \(C\) such that
\[
 \sup_{\boldsymbol d,\vartheta}
 \left|Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta;\widehat g_A)
 -Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta;g_0)\right|
 \leq C\|\widehat g_A-g_0\|_2+
 \|W\|_2\|\widehat g_A-g_0\|_2^2=o_p(1). \tag{30}
\]
The true graph has population minimum zero.  Every wrong graph has minimum at least
\(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0\).  Hence (30), finiteness of \(\mathfrak G\), and the fixed graph tie order imply
\[
 \Pr(\widehat{\boldsymbol D}=\boldsymbol D_0)\longrightarrow1. \tag{31}
\]

On the true graph, \(\mathrm{lem{:}certified\text{-}global\text{-}identification}\) makes \(\theta_0\) the unique population minimizer.  The inference-split analogue of (30) and the frozen \(\mathrm{lem{:}extremum\text{-}consistency}\) give \(\widehat\theta\to_p\theta_0\) on the event in (31).  The assumptions \(\theta_0\in\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol D_0}\) and certified positive clearance imply that this exact global minimizer is interior with probability tending to one.  Put
\(J_0=J_{\boldsymbol D_0,\mathcal T}(\theta_0)\).  The certified Jacobian margin gives full column rank of \(J_0\); since \(W\succ0\), \(J_0^{\mathsf T}WJ_0\) is invertible.  The frozen \(\mathrm{lem{:}minimum\text{-}distance\text{-}normality}\), applied to (29), yields
\[
 \sqrt{N_B}(\widehat\theta-\theta_0)
 =(J_0^{\mathsf T}WJ_0)^{-1}J_0^{\mathsf T}W
 \sqrt{N_B}(\widehat g_B-g_0)+o_p(1), \tag{32}
\]
whose covariance is exactly \(V_\theta(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0)\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}sandwich\text{-}covariance}\).

The graph-selection event uses only the training split and is independent of the inference split.  For any bounded continuous test function, replacing the selected estimator by the true-graph estimator changes its expectation by at most twice the function bound times \(\Pr(\widehat{\boldsymbol D}\ne\boldsymbol D_0)\).  Equation (31) therefore transfers (32) to the unconditional selected estimator.  Twice continuous differentiability of the fixed truncated-factorization contrast and a first-order expansion give
\[
 \sqrt{N_B}(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}-\boldsymbol\tau)
 =C_\tau(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0;\iota)
 \sqrt{N_B}(\widehat\theta-\theta_0)+o_p(1),
\]
and hence the asserted normal limit with covariance
\(V_\tau(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0;\iota)\).

The empirical same-well products consistently estimate every \(\Omega_j\) by the stratified PGF lemma.  The row fractions and recovered moments are consistent, and all matrix inverses are evaluated on a certified nonsingular neighborhood.  Continuity of finite matrix products and inverses therefore proves plug-in consistency for \(\Sigma_g\), \(V_\theta\), and \(V_\tau\).  The contrast-nondegeneracy assumption makes each reported scalar limit variance \(\sigma^2\) strictly positive.  To verify studentization directly, let \(X_N\) denote one centered, scaled contrast and let \(\widehat\sigma_N\to_p\sigma\).  For \(0<\epsilon<1\), outside an event of probability tending to zero, \(\widehat\sigma_N/\sigma\in[1-\epsilon,1+\epsilon]\).  The distribution function of \(X_N/\widehat\sigma_N\) is consequently squeezed between those of \(X_N/\{\sigma(1-\epsilon)\}\) and \(X_N/\{\sigma(1+\epsilon)\}\), with the inequalities reversed when the threshold is negative.  The established normal limit, followed by \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) and continuity of the standard normal distribution, proves convergence of the studentized statistic to \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).  Its symmetric normal-quantile interval therefore has pointwise coverage \(1-\alpha\).  No uniform coverage claim at a graph, parameter-box, or zero-variance boundary is made.

Finally, spectral submultiplicativity and \(A_{\mathcal T}=M^+\otimes I_L\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|\Sigma_g\|_2
 &\leq\|D_g\|_2^2\|A_{\mathcal T}\|_2^2
 \|D_h^{-1}\|_2^2\|\Sigma_h\|_2\\
 &=\|\operatorname{diag}(g)\|_2^2\|M^+\|_2^2
 \|\operatorname{diag}(h)^{-1}\|_2^2\|\Sigma_h\|_2,
\end{aligned}
\]
because the singular values of \(M^+\otimes I_L\) are those of \(M^+\), each repeated \(L\) times.  Positivity of all PGF coordinates justifies \(D_h^{-1}\).  This is the claimed pooling-amplification bound.

statements.justification: This checks the general inverse against the smallest genuinely mixed full-rank design.
statements.gap: The calculation is a sanity reduction and is not presented as a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It provides an auditable population inverse for the synthetic two-type application.
statements.proof_tex:
The fixed matrix has determinant \(1\), so it is invertible and its Moore--Penrose inverse is its ordinary inverse:
\[
M_0^+=M_0^{-1}
=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The rank-frontier identity gives
\[
\begin{pmatrix}\log G_1\\ \log G_2\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\log H_1\\ \log H_2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
All PGFs are strictly positive on \((0,1]^p\), so exponentiation and ordinary division are valid and yield
\[
G_1=\frac{H_1^2}{H_2},\qquad G_2=\frac{H_2}{H_1}.
\]

statements.statement: Run \(\mathfrak C\) on the complete rational input \(\Xi_0\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}fixed\text{-}protocol}\). If and only if its status is \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\), run it once more on the uniquely prescribed replacement \(\Xi_1=\mathfrak F_0(\Xi_0)\); do not refine after \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) or \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\). Does one of these two runs return \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\), thereby proving positive nonvacuous wrong-graph, Jacobian, remote-identification, and local-injectivity bounds, valid tails, and \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq200000\) for the synthetic \(p=3\), \((i_X,i_Y,i_Z)=(1,2,3)\) benchmark?
statements.justification: This is a falsifiable application of the reusable procedure, not the headline theorem and not evidence for an existing biological assay.
statements.gap: The floating-point pilot checks only two local witness Jacobians and no wrong-graph boxes; it does not establish any uniform premise used by the inference theorem.
statements.consumer: A certified answer licenses only the stated synthetic prospective benchmark; a collision, singularity, or precision obstruction stops that protocol without affecting the rank frontier.

obligation.what_is_open: Neither prescribed run of \(\mathfrak C\) has a supplied validated proof object, so the tri-valued status of \(\Xi_0\), and conditionally of \(\Xi_1\), is not derivable from the frozen records.
obligation.obstruction: The certificate theorem proves soundness of a completed directed-rounding record; it does not manufacture the millions of box, tail, chart, covariance, and precision receipts required for this concrete input. Floating-point witness singular values do not lower-bound the full compact graph boxes.
obligation.attempted: The exact rank, inverse, full-support model check, and intervention arithmetic close symbolically. The remaining wrong-graph, remote-pair, chart, tail, and variance tests depend on executing the literal finite procedure with outward rounding.
obligation.partial_result: The frozen definitions prove \(\operatorname{rank}(M_0)=2\), the exact inverse \(G_1=H_1^2/H_2\), and witness contrasts \((3,25)\) for both types.  They do not contain a directed-rounding proof object \(\Pi_{\mathrm{cert}}\) for either \(\Xi_0\) or \(\Xi_1\).  The reported floating-point singular values are point evaluations and do not certify any uniform wrong-graph, remote-identification, local-chart, tail, or precision inequality.

statements.statement: If \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)\) returns \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\), its recorded valid cover \(\mathscr C\) satisfies \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)\geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}>0\), so every same-graph pair closer than \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) is separated in a co-containing chart. Every feasible pair at least \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) apart has squared \(W\)-distance at least \(\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}>0\), with the remote claim vacuous when that pair set is empty. Therefore every \(m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}\) is globally injective on \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\), and \(Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\cdot;m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta_0))\) has unique minimum \(\theta_0\) with the certified remote separation outside its local neighborhood.
statements.justification: This prevents local Jacobian rank from substituting for global uniqueness.
statements.gap: A local inverse theorem alone does not certify a unique compact-box population minimum.
statements.consumer: It supplies the global identification premise for the deterministic minimum-distance estimator.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\boldsymbol d\) and suppose
\(m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta)=m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta')\).  If \(\|\theta-\theta'\|_2<r_{\mathrm{id}}\), validity of the recorded cover puts both parameters in a common chart \(C_{\boldsymbol d c}\).  Equality of the moment vectors implies equality after projection, while certification gives
\[
 0=\langle\phi_{\boldsymbol d c}(\theta)-
 \phi_{\boldsymbol d c}(\theta'),\theta-\theta'\rangle
 \geq \underline\mu_{\mathcal T}\|\theta-\theta'\|_2^2. \tag{18}
\]
Because \(\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}>0\), (18) forces \(\theta=\theta'\).  If their distance is at least \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\), the certified remote bound instead gives
\[
 \|m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta)-
 m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta')\|_W^2
 \geq\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}>0, \tag{19}
\]
contradicting equality.  When the remote feasible set is empty this second case cannot occur.  The moment map is therefore globally injective.

For \(g_0=m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta_0)\), positive definiteness of \(W\) and the injectivity just proved yield
\[
 Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta;g_0)=0
 \Longleftrightarrow
 m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta)=g_0
 \Longleftrightarrow \theta=\theta_0. \tag{20}
\]
Thus \(\theta_0\) is the unique compact-box minimizer, and (19) supplies the claimed quantitative separation outside its local neighborhood.

statements.statement: For every finite admissible design class, the certified Pareto frontier is exactly computable by finite enumeration, certified infeasibility pruning, and certified dominance pruning.  A candidate may be discarded without running its remaining certificate tasks whenever a proved upper envelope for all of its attainable objective coordinates is weakly dominated, with one strict coordinate, by the proved lower objective vector of an already certified candidate.  After all unpruned candidates terminate, pairwise comparison of their certified output vectors returns exactly \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{adm}}\).  No assumption in the frozen core guarantees a strict reduction from exhaustive evaluation in the worst case: all admissible candidates can remain feasible and mutually nondominated.
statements.proof_tex:
The caps make \(\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{adm}}\) finite.  Indeed there are finitely many choices of \(J\), finitely many matrices in \(\{0,\ldots,m_{\max}\}^{J\times K}\), finitely many nonempty grid subsets of the finite set \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{cand}}\) with size at most \(L_{\max}\), finitely many declared allocations and well caps, and finitely many integer truncation, moment, Taylor, subdivision, and precision choices under \(\mathfrak b\).  The constraint \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\leq B_{\max}\) only removes candidates.  Write the resulting set as \(\{\Xi_1,\ldots,\Xi_N\}\).

For a certified candidate define the maximization-oriented vector
\[
 y(\Xi)=\bigl(\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T},
 \underline\kappa_{\mathcal T},
 \underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T},
 \underline\mu_{\mathcal T},
 -N_{\mathrm{req}},-w_{\mathrm{cert}},-\mathfrak B(\Xi)\bigr). \tag{33}
\]
Order candidates by their finite encodings.  First apply the exact syntax, rank, simplex, box, and arithmetic-cap tests.  Maintain the set \(C\) of completed certified candidates.  If interval calculations for an unfinished candidate \(x\) prove an upper envelope \(U(x)\) satisfying \(y(x)\preceq U(x)\) for every possible certified completion, and some \(c\in C\) satisfies \(y(c)\succeq U(x)\) with one strict coordinate, discard \(x\).  This is sound because transitivity gives \(y(c)\succeq y(x)\) with a strict coordinate.  Otherwise run the remaining finite certificate tasks.  When all unpruned candidates have terminated, delete from \(C\) each candidate dominated by another member of \(C\).

The one-sided conclusions of \(\mathrm{thm{:}certificate\text{-}soundness\text{-}complexity}\) validate every infeasibility decision and every bound used in this comparison.  A pruned candidate cannot be Pareto maximal.  Every retained candidate is certified and is not dominated by any certified candidate, because the final comparison is exhaustive over all certified, unpruned completions.  Conversely, a certified nondominated candidate can be neither soundly infeasible nor soundly dominated by an envelope, so it survives.  The returned set is exactly \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{adm}}\).

Nothing in the frozen assumptions forces a candidate to be infeasible or dominated before its certificate tasks are evaluated.  For an explicit generic-class certificate, take an admissible instance whose finite candidate sets and caps leave a singleton \(\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{adm}}=\{\Xi\}\) and for which \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)=\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\).  Its frontier is \(\{\Xi\}\), and its only candidate must undergo the tests establishing certification.  More generally, if all certified vectors (33) are pairwise incomparable, dominance pruning removes none.  Therefore the algorithm is exact and its pruning rules can be useful, but no strict worst-case reduction from exhaustive evaluation follows without an additional structural dominance theorem.
