statements.statement: On every fixed graph box in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), all count moments are finite uniformly over the box; the joint mass function, every component PGF on \((0,1)^p\), and every fixed truncated-factorization contrast are twice continuously differentiable in the coefficients, with differentiation permitted term by term.  For each fixed graph tuple, the coefficient-to-law map is injective and has injective differential at every coefficient vector.  The compact law images of two distinct graph tuples are disjoint.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a graph tuple \(\boldsymbol d\).  It suffices to work type by type because the parameter blocks of distinct types are disjoint.  Choose a topological ordering.  At a root, every moment of \(V_s\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\alpha_s)\) is a polynomial in \(\alpha_s\), hence is uniformly bounded on the compact coefficient box.  If the claim is known for all predecessors of a non-root \(s\), then for every integer \(m\geq0\),
\[
 \mathbb E_\theta[V_s^m\mid V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)}]
 =\sum_{k=0}^{m}
 \left\{\begin{matrix}m\\ k\end{matrix}\right\}
 \lambda_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})^k. \tag{4}
\]
The rate is a fixed polynomial in predecessor counts and its coefficients are uniformly bounded on \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\).  Expansion of its powers and H\"older's inequality reduce the expectation of every term in (4) to finitely many predecessor moments.  Topological induction therefore proves
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}}
 \mathbb E_\theta\!\left[\left(1+\sum_{s=1}^pV_s\right)^m\right]<\infty
 \qquad(m\in\mathbb N_0). \tag{5}
\]
The same induction applies after fixing the intervention coordinate at \(1\) or \(2\).

Every rate has a uniform positive lower bound on the box.  If \(t\) indexes the intercept or an edge coefficient in the rate of node \(s\), write
\[
 a_{st}(v_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})
 \in\{1,v_k^{q_{sk}}:k\in\operatorname{pa}(s)\}.
\]
For the positive joint mass \(p_\theta(v)\), direct differentiation gives
\[
 \partial_t\log p_\theta(v)=
 a_{st}(v_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})
 \left\{\frac{v_s}{\lambda_s(v_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})}-1\right\}. \tag{6}
\]
First and second parameter derivatives of \(p_\theta(v)\) are consequently bounded in absolute value by \(p_\theta(v)\) times a fixed polynomial in \(v\), uniformly over the box.  This gives the needed uniform summability without silently invoking a pointwise dominating law: if that polynomial has degree \(d\), then for any \(a\geq1\), (5) and Markov's inequality give
\[
 \sup_\theta\sum_{\sum_s v_s>R}
 |\partial^\nu p_\theta(v)|
 \leq \frac{C}{R^a}
 \sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta
 \left(1+\sum_sV_s\right)^{d+a}
 \longrightarrow0,
 \qquad |\nu|\leq2. \tag{7}
\]
Thus the derivative series are uniformly Cauchy.  Termwise differentiation on each finite truncation followed by (7) proves twice continuous differentiability of the joint mass, every PGF on \((0,1)^p\), and every fixed intervened first-moment contrast.  Equation (5) also proves finiteness of all moments uniformly on the box.

The positive observational law determines every conditional mean at every parent vector.  Hence it determines
\[
 \lambda_s(x)=\mathbb E_\theta[V_s\mid V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)}=x],
 \qquad
 \alpha_s=\lambda_s(0),
 \qquad
 b_{sk}=\lambda_s(e_k)-\lambda_s(0), \tag{8}
\]
where \(e_k\) has its \(k\)-coordinate equal to one and its other coordinates zero.  This proves injectivity of the coefficient-to-law map within a fixed graph.

For differential injectivity, group the scores from (6) by node:
\[
 S_s=f_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})
 \frac{V_s-\lambda_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})}
 {\lambda_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})},
 \qquad
 f_s=\bigl(1,(V_k^{q_{sk}})_{k\in\operatorname{pa}(s)}\bigr)^{\mathsf T}. \tag{9}
\]
In the topological filtration, each \(S_s\) has conditional mean zero given all preceding variables.  Hence different node blocks are orthogonal, while the information block for node \(s\) is
\[
 I_s=\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[\frac{f_sf_s^{\mathsf T}}{\lambda_s}\right]. \tag{10}
\]
If \(c^{\mathsf T}I_sc=0\), positivity of \(\lambda_s\) and full support from \(\mathrm{prop{:}polynomial\text{-}class\text{-}inclusion}\) imply \(c^{\mathsf T}f_s(x)=0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb N_0^{|\operatorname{pa}(s)|}\).  Evaluation at zero and then at each coordinate unit vector forces all entries of \(c\) to vanish.  Thus every block in (10) is positive definite.  For every nonzero full parameter direction \(a\),
\[
 \mathbb E_\theta[(a^{\mathsf T}S)^2]>0. \tag{11}
\]

Suppose the directional derivative of the PGF vanished on a nonempty open subset of \((0,1)^p\).  By (7), it is the absolutely convergent signed power series
\[
 \sum_{v\in\mathbb N_0^p}p_\theta(v)a^{\mathsf T}S(v)z^v. \tag{12}
\]
Successively fix all but one coordinate.  Here is the needed one-variable argument.  If a power series vanishes on an open subinterval of its convergence interval, all derivatives vanish at an interior point, so its Taylor expansion vanishes on a neighborhood of that point.  Overlapping convergence neighborhoods continue the zero identity through \((0,1)\).  If a coefficient were nonzero, choose its least index \(m\); division by \(z^m\) and passage to \(z\downarrow0\) would give that coefficient equal to zero, a contradiction.  Thus every coefficient vanishes.  Iterating this argument over the \(p\) coordinates makes every coefficient in (12) zero.  Since \(p_\theta(v)>0\), this would make \(a^{\mathsf T}S(v)=0\) for all \(v\), contradicting (11).  The coefficient-to-law differential is therefore injective.

Finally, \(\mathrm{prop{:}polynomial\text{-}class\text{-}inclusion}\) puts every displayed law in the pairwise-identifiable CPCM class, and the frozen \(\mathrm{lem{:}cpcm\text{-}dag\text{-}identification}\) gives a unique labeled generating DAG.  Thus two distinct labeled graph tuples have disjoint law images.  Coordinatewise continuity of the mass functions and compactness of the coefficient boxes make each image compact in the product topology on probability masses.  This proves all assertions, including their finite stacking over types.

statements.statement:
Under full column rank and the positive stable row allocation, for either sample split with total size \(N\),
\[
\sqrt N(\widehat h-h)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_h),
\qquad
\sqrt N(\widehat g-g)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_g),
\]
where \(\Sigma_h,\Sigma_g\) are those in \(\mathrm{def{:}replicate\text{-}pgf\text{-}covariance}\).  The same-well cross-grid entries are
\[
(\Omega_j)_{\ell\ell'}
=H_j(z_\ell\odot z_{\ell'})
-H_j(z_\ell)H_j(z_{\ell'}).
\]
Replacing the expectations, row fractions, and recovered moments by their empirical analogues gives a consistent plug-in covariance estimator.
statements.proof_tex:
For row \(j\), define the bounded vector
\[
U_{ji}=(z_\ell^{B_{ji}})_{\ell=1}^L,\qquad
\widehat h_j=\frac1{n_j}\sum_{i=1}^{n_j}U_{ji}.
\]
Its mean is \(h_j=(H_j(z_\ell))_\ell\).  Because
\[
z_\ell^{B_{ji}}z_{\ell'}^{B_{ji}}
=(z_\ell\odot z_{\ell'})^{B_{ji}},
\]
its covariance is exactly \(\Omega_j\) as displayed in the claim.  The bounded-vector central limit theorem gives
\[
\sqrt{n_j}(\widehat h_j-h_j)\Rightarrow
\mathcal N(0,\Omega_j).
\]
The row samples are independent, and \(n_j/N\to\rho_j>0\).  Stacking the finitely many rows and multiplying row \(j\) by
\(\sqrt{N/n_j}\) therefore gives
\[
\sqrt N(\widehat h-h)\Rightarrow
\mathcal N\!\left(0,
\operatorname{blockdiag}(\Omega_j/\rho_j)_{j=1}^J\right)
=\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_h). \tag{5}
\]

Every coordinate of \(h\) is strictly positive because every integrand \(z_\ell^{B_{ji}}\) is strictly positive.  On the positive orthant define
\[
F(x)=\exp\{A_{\mathcal T}\log x\},
\qquad A_{\mathcal T}=M^+\otimes I_L.
\]
Full column rank and the rank-frontier identity give \(F(h)=g\), while
\[
DF(h)=D_gA_{\mathcal T}D_h^{-1}. \tag{6}
\]
Applying the differentiable-map part of the cited finite-vector limit result to (5) and (6) yields
\[
\Sigma_g
=D_gA_{\mathcal T}D_h^{-1}\Sigma_h
D_h^{-1}A_{\mathcal T}^{\mathsf T}D_g,
\]
which is the declared covariance.

For consistency, every coordinate of the empirical first and second products is an average of bounded variables.  Its variance is \(O(n_j^{-1})\), so Chebyshev's inequality gives convergence in probability.  Since \(n_j/N\to\rho_j>0\), empirical row fractions converge as well.  Matrix multiplication, coordinatewise logarithm on the positive orthant, and the diagonal maps are continuous; hence substitution in (5)--(6) consistently estimates both covariance matrices.

statements.statement:
Fix the substantive finite design data in \(\Xi\), including \(M,\iota,\mathcal T,\mathfrak G,(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d},\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol d}),q,W,\rho,r_{\mathrm{id}},\alpha,w_{\max}\), and \(N_{\max}\), and consider a sequence \((\Xi_t)\) that changes only the truncation, Taylor, subdivision, and outward-rounding controls.  Define the exact worst-case contrast variance and its exact well requirement by
\[
 v_\tau^\circ=\max_{\boldsymbol d\in\mathfrak G}
 \max_{\theta\in\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol d}}
 \max_{1\leq a\leq2K}
 [V_\tau(\boldsymbol d,\theta;\iota)]_{aa},
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{req}}^\circ=
 z_{1-\alpha/2}^2v_\tau^\circ/w_{\max}^2.
\]
Suppose the exact syntax and box tests pass, \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), every \(\rho_j>0\), and there are strict positive uniform exact margins for every nonempty wrong-graph comparison, every nonempty remote within-graph comparison, every required local chart strong-monotonicity and Jacobian test, every required interiority, denominator, and positive-definiteness test, and the contrast-precision inequality \(N_{\mathrm{req}}^\circ<N_{\max}\).  If the Poisson-tail errors, Taylor-enclosure widths, terminal objective and chart mesh diameters, and outward-rounding errors all converge uniformly to zero, and the deterministic chart trees eventually give a valid cover with the stated local margin, then \(\mathfrak C(\Xi_t)=\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) for all sufficiently large \(t\).  This is a relative eventual-certification result; it does not assert that either prescribed synthetic benchmark satisfies its strict-slack or convergence hypotheses.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix the substantive entries of \(\Xi\) and the sequence \((\Xi_t)\) from the statement.  All graph-specific parameter boxes and their pairwise products are compact, and there are only finitely many graph tuples.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}polynomial\text{-}pgf\text{-}regularity}\), the exact moment maps and all derivatives used by the procedure are continuous on these boxes.  The stipulated positive denominator and positive-definiteness margins make the exact covariance, sandwich, and contrast-variance maps continuous on the inference boxes as well.  The assumed uniform convergence of the tail errors, Taylor-enclosure widths, terminal mesh diameters, and outward-rounding errors therefore implies the following common enclosure property: there is a deterministic sequence \(e_t\downarrow0\) such that every lower endpoint used at stage \(t\) is at least the infimum of its exact scalar target over the relevant leaf minus \(e_t\), and every upper endpoint is at most the corresponding supremum plus \(e_t\).  The analogous operator-norm excess for every required matrix enclosure is at most \(e_t\).  Enlarging \(e_t\) by a fixed finite factor if necessary covers all finitely many kinds of tests.

Let \(\gamma_*>0\) be a common lower bound for the exact wrong-graph objectives on all nonempty wrong-graph comparison products.  Such a number exists by the strict uniform graph-separation hypothesis and finiteness of \(\mathfrak G\).  If
\[
 f_{\boldsymbol d,\boldsymbol d'}(\vartheta,\vartheta')
 =\left\lVert m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta)
        -m_{\boldsymbol d',\mathcal T}(\vartheta')\right\rVert_W^2,
\]
then \(f_{\boldsymbol d,\boldsymbol d'}\geq\gamma_*\) on every such product.  Consequently, once \(e_t<\gamma_*/2\), every wrong-graph leaf has a strictly positive lower enclosure and passes.  When there is no wrong-graph comparison, both the exact and certified graph bounds are \(+\infty\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}grid\text{-}criterion}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}procedure}\), so no numerical test is required.

We next prove eventual success of the remote-pair branch without asserting a uniform negative distance margin merely from membership in the open set \(\{D<0\}\).  Fix a graph \(\boldsymbol d\), put
\[
 K_{\boldsymbol d}=\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\times\Theta_{\boldsymbol d},
 \qquad
 D(\vartheta,\vartheta')=\lVert\vartheta-\vartheta'\rVert_2^2-r_{\mathrm{id}}^2,
\]
and define
\[
 f(\vartheta,\vartheta')=
 \left\lVert m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta)
              -m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta')\right\rVert_W^2,
 \qquad
 S=\{x\in K_{\boldsymbol d}:D(x)\geq0\}.
\]
First suppose \(S\neq\varnothing\).  The strict uniform remote slack supplies \(\lambda_*>0\), common over the finitely many nonempty remote tasks, such that
\[
 f(x)\geq\lambda_*\qquad(x\in S).
\]
Let
\[
 U=\{x\in K_{\boldsymbol d}:f(x)>\lambda_*/2\}.
\]
Continuity of \(f\) makes \(U\) relatively open in \(K_{\boldsymbol d}\), and the preceding inequality gives \(S\subset U\).  Hence the complement \(C=K_{\boldsymbol d}\setminus U\) is compact and disjoint from \(S\).  Thus \(D<0\) on \(C\).  If \(C\neq\varnothing\), continuity and compactness give the genuine uniform separation
\[
 \delta_{\boldsymbol d}:=-\max_{x\in C}D(x)>0,
 \qquad D(x)\leq-\delta_{\boldsymbol d}\quad(x\in C).
\]
This margin is obtained on the compact complement \(C\), not on the whole open set \(\{D<0\}\).  Uniform continuity of \(D\) on \(K_{\boldsymbol d}\) yields \(a_{\boldsymbol d}>0\) such that
\[
 \lVert x-y\rVert_2<a_{\boldsymbol d}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 |D(x)-D(y)|<\delta_{\boldsymbol d}/2.
\]
Consider any closed terminal product leaf \(B\subset K_{\boldsymbol d}\) with diameter below \(a_{\boldsymbol d}\).  If \(B\cap C=\varnothing\), then \(B\subset U\), whence \(f>\lambda_*/2\) throughout \(B\); for \(e_t<\lambda_*/4\), its moment-distance lower enclosure is positive and the corrected branch rule passes \(B\), whether or not \(B\) straddles \(D=0\).  If \(B\cap C\neq\varnothing\), choose \(x\in B\cap C\).  For every \(y\in B\),
\[
 D(y)\leq D(x)+|D(y)-D(x)|
 <-\delta_{\boldsymbol d}/2.
\]
For \(e_t<\delta_{\boldsymbol d}/4\), the upper enclosure of \(D\) on \(B\) is therefore negative, so the branch discards \(B\).  If \(C=\varnothing\), every leaf is contained in \(U\) and the first case alone applies.  This gives the required finite-cover/mesh argument: once the terminal mesh is smaller than the minimum of the finitely many positive \(a_{\boldsymbol d}\), every leaf lies in the passing case or meets a compact set on which the distance constraint has the displayed negative margin and hence lies in the discard case.  If instead \(S=\varnothing\), compactness directly gives \(\max_{K_{\boldsymbol d}}D=-\delta_{\boldsymbol d}<0\), so all sufficiently accurate leaves are discarded and the remote bound is \(+\infty\).  It follows that every remote tree eventually terminates successfully under precisely the corrected remote-subset rule in \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}procedure}\).

For the local tests, let \(\mu_*>0\) and \(\kappa_*>0\) be common lower bounds for the stipulated exact chart strong-monotonicity margins and Jacobian singular values.  The deterministic chart trees are assumed eventually to produce a valid cover.  On every resulting chart, the exact symmetric projected-Jacobian matrix has least eigenvalue at least \(\mu_*\), while
\[
 J_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta)^{\mathsf T}
 J_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta)
 \succeq \kappa_*^2 I.
\]
Uniform derivative-enclosure and rounding convergence makes the corresponding interval \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) tests succeed for all sufficiently large \(t\).  Indeed, one may fix positive dyadic numbers strictly below \(\mu_*\) and \(\kappa_*\); the arithmetic-precision mesh eventually contains such test values, and the uniform matrix-enclosure error is eventually smaller than their slack.  The eventual valid-cover hypothesis then supplies the required coverage and co-containment checks.  The same argument, applied to the strict uniform interiority, denominator, pivot, and positive-definiteness margins in the statement, makes every remaining algebraic and covariance test succeed.  The exact rank computation succeeds because \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), and the allocation checks succeed because \(\rho\in\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) and every \(\rho_j>0\).

It remains to verify the precision check.  Compactness of the inference boxes and continuity of \(V_\tau\) show that the maximum defining \(v_\tau^\circ\) is finite and attained.  Put
\[
 s_*=N_{\max}-N_{\mathrm{req}}^\circ>0.
\]
Uniform convergence of the covariance, derivative, matrix-inverse, and contrast enclosures implies that the recorded variance upper bound \(\max_a(\overline v_\tau)_a\) converges from above to \(v_\tau^\circ\).  Since \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and \(w_{\max}>0\) are fixed, the map
\[
 v\longmapsto z_{1-\alpha/2}^2v/w_{\max}^2
\]
is continuous.  Therefore, for all sufficiently large \(t\),
\[
 N_{\mathrm{req}}(\Xi_t)
 <N_{\mathrm{req}}^\circ+s_*/2
 <N_{\max}.
\]

There are finitely many graph tuples and test categories, so the preceding thresholds have a common finite index \(t_0\).  For every \(t\geq t_0\), the syntax and box checks, full-rank and positive-allocation checks, all graph, remote, chart, covariance, interiority, and linear-algebra checks, and the required-well check pass.  The literal return rule in \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}procedure}\) therefore gives
\[
 \mathfrak C(\Xi_t)=\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\qquad(t\geq t_0).
\]
This conclusion is consistent with the unconditional finite termination and one-sided soundness of \(\mathrm{thm{:}certificate\text{-}soundness\text{-}complexity}\).  The proof uses the theorem's stated strict-slack and uniform-convergence hypotheses only; it does not establish them for either prescribed synthetic benchmark.
statements.justification: This is the precise relative completeness counterpart to the unconditional finite-termination and one-sided-soundness theorem.
statements.gap: Finite interval procedures need not certify at fixed controls; eventual success follows only from strict exact slack and uniform convergence of every enclosure and mesh used by the return rule.
statements.consumer: It explains when increasing declared numerical controls will eventually turn a genuinely separated prospective design into a certified one, without asserting that either synthetic benchmark qualifies.

statements.statement: For \(p\geq 2\), consider a pooled experiment in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\). If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\) and \(((P_r,D_r))_{r=1}^{K}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\), then the observed pooled-law tuple \(\mathscr A_M((P_r)_{r=1}^{K})\) identifies every labeled component law \(P_r\) and every labeled generating DAG \(D_r\).
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(H_j(z)=\mathbb E[z^{B_{ji}}]\) be the PGF of composition row \(j\), and write \(H(z)=(H_1(z),\ldots,H_J(z))^{\mathsf T}\). Membership of the experiment in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\), whose defining hypotheses are those used in \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}frontier}\), gives
\[
 \log H(z)=M(\log G_1(z),\ldots,\log G_K(z))^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad z\in(0,1]^p.
\]
Because \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), the same theorem gives the observable inverse
\[
 (G_1(z),\ldots,G_K(z))^{\mathsf T}
 =\exp\{M^+\log H(z)\}. \tag{1}
\]
PGF coefficient uniqueness, also supplied by \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}frontier}\), therefore identifies each full joint law \(P_r\). The coordinate in (1) indexed by \(r\) is tied to column \(r\) of the fixed known matrix \(M\), so this inversion preserves the type labels rather than identifying the laws only up to permutation.

For each \(r\), membership in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\) states that \(P_r\) is generated by a causally minimal, pairwise-identifiable count-valued CPCM with labeled DAG \(D_r\). The cited \(\mathrm{lem{:}cpcm\text{-}dag\text{-}identification}\), which is Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin's Lemma 11, says that the generating DAG of such a direct joint law is identifiable from that law. Applying it to the already identified \(P_r\), separately for \(r=1,\ldots,K\), identifies every \(D_r\). No ordered three-coordinate embedding, polynomial rate restriction, or intervention premise is used in this argument.
statements.justification: This theorem isolates the direct-law CPCM step from the intervention layer: after full-rank labeled unpooling, Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin's Lemma 11 applies already for \(p\geq2\).
statements.gap: The published CPCM theorem starts from one directly observed joint law; it does not invert several known-composition aggregate laws or preserve cell-type labels through that inversion.
statements.consumer: It gives prospective bulk designs a broad labeled-DAG guarantee without imposing Poisson source laws, polynomial rates, or a three-coordinate intervention embedding.
